repair_hint: 1) LEAK in HL: Remove or reframe the reliability inference. The phrase 'that kind of sloppiness in docs usually means the library itself is unreliable' is a case-level severity claim about the user's SDK, not merely a credibility signal about the source. Option A: delete the inference entirely ('...told me they had reviewed the same vendor SDK documentation — typos everywhere and broken formatting throughout'). Option B: recast it unambiguously as the source's personal general belief detached from the user's case, but even then a smart responder would apply it to the case — deletion is safer. 2) HH/LH non-equivalence: LH omits several factual claims that HH makes — specifically: (a) the SDK dispatch proceeds normally before the crash, (b) the crash is three frames deep inside the callback, (c) the specific operation is a write to a shared mutable dictionary without a lock, (d) all three stack traces are identical. Expand LH to flatly state these same claims, e.g.: 'The crash stack trace ends inside our own callback code, not in the SDK; across all three occurrences the traces are identical and terminate while writing to a shared dictionary without a lock.'
